result:
The FEBio queue is busy again after sitting idle from 14:15 to 20:36. I changed no settings. One job, physrot2_p001, failed and needs a person to look at it.

- **Running:** a new batch of 39 physio_rot_r2 runs was queued at 20:36. 12 are running: 10 on GPUs 1–6 and 2 on CPU only. 27 are waiting; the oldest has waited 14 minutes. Every run's log grew in the last 9 seconds, so nothing is hung. None of the new runs has finished yet (the oldest is 13 minutes in).
- **Limiting resource:** CPU. Load is 31.5 against the 32-core quota, and the CPU was throttled in 77% of time slices over a 10-second check. The 12 runs claim 4 cores each, which is the scheduler's 1.5× overcommit limit, so it won't start more.
- **Spare capacity:** the GPUs are mostly lightly used. Memory shows 126.9 of 128 GiB in use, but 93.5 GiB of that is file cache the system can free; actual process memory is 31.8 GiB. No new out-of-memory kills (still 2, both old). I didn't raise concurrency because the CPU is already the bottleneck.
- **physrot2_p001 failed (20:46):** its job points to `physio_rot_r2/p001`, which doesn't exist. The case is in `physio_rot_r2_p001try/`. I didn't re-queue it because the path is wrong, not a crash. Whoever owns physio_rot_r2 should either fix the job or drop it. I don't know who queued it.
- **Next hour:** with this much throttling, the runs may each take noticeably longer than the earlier batch. If they do, I'll lower the overcommit from 1.5 back to 1.25, but only after measuring.
- **Services:** all background (tmux) sessions are up. The evo task queue is empty, and the 5 failed gate2 tasks there are from 10-28.
